articles.title: Vulnerability remediation: Match CVEs to asset owners in seconds with Tenable Hexa AI
articles.summary: CopyFail drops and it's a doozy — CVE-2026-31431 lets any schmuck with local access become root on most Linux boxes. Microsoft's suddenly very helpful with the disclosure, which is either refreshingly responsible or hilariously ironic.

articles.title: Trellix Confirms Source Code Breach With Unauthorized Repository Access
articles.summary: CISA fast-tracks that Linux root escalation bug to their Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list because apparently script kiddies don't waste time. When CISA moves this fast, you know the wild is already very, very wild.

articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Meanwhile Chrome notches its fourth zero-day of the year because apparently we're speed-running browser exploits now.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability gets weaponized before patches even land, with ransomware gangs already cashing in. When millions of sites share the same admin panel, one bug becomes everyone's very bad day.

articles.title: CVE-2026-31431: Copy Fail vulnerability enables Linux root privilege escalation across cloud environments
articles.summary: French 15-year-old allegedly hacks the national ID agency and tries to flip millions of citizen records on the dark web. Gen Z really said 'hold my energy drink' to traditional cybercrime career paths.

articles.title: 30,000 Facebook Accounts Hacked via Google AppSheet Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Trellix admits to source code breach with the corporate equivalent of 'we recently identified' — translation: we got owned and hope nobody notices the crown jewels walking out the door. Cybersecurity company self-owns are always *chef's kiss*.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: Public records laws expose the surveillance state's license plate tracking empire, so naturally states want to classify what citizens can see. FOIA wins are making ALPR dystopia visible, and the panopticon doesn't like the spotlight.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's anti-VPN law goes live next week because nothing says 'freedom' like mandating digital strip searches. Cue the predictable VPN usage surge as residents remember what privacy feels like.

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: UK's cyber agency warns AI is about to unleash a 'patch tsunami' by finding decades of buried code debt all at once. Technical shortcuts are coming home to roost, and the bill's arriving with compound interest.

articles.title: A Bridge to Somewhere: How to Link Your Mastodon, Bluesky, or Other Federated Accounts
articles.summary: Germany doxes 'UNKN,' the mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware operations that terrorized the internet. Daniil Shchukin's face reveal marks the end of an era when ransomware kingpins could hide behind handles.
